Create an admiral_df Dataset

Source: R/admiral_df.R
admiral_df.Rd

Tags a data frame with the admiral_df class and stores its metadata: the key variables – the variables which uniquely identify its records – the dataset name, and the ADaM dataset class. Call it on the finished dataset, once it has been derived, e.g. just before summarizing it: the metadata is not guaranteed to survive the derivations which build the dataset (see Details). The metadata is read back with get_dataset_keys(), get_dataset_name(), and get_dataset_class().

Called on a dataset which is already an admiral_df, it updates the metadata rather than rebuilding it: an argument left as NULL keeps the value stored by the previous call, so each item can be set on its own.

The keys describe the record structure the dataset is intended to have; they are not checked against its records when they are stored. {admiral} never infers the keys of a dataset: if they have not been set with this function, functions which need them ask for them to be set. The class, by contrast, is inferred from the dataset if it has not been set (see infer_dataset_class()), but a class set here always takes precedence.

Usage

admiral_df(
  dataset,
  dataset_keys = NULL,
  dataset_name = NULL,
  dataset_class = NULL
)

Arguments

dataset

A data frame. It does not need to have the admiral_df class already; the class is added if it is missing.

Permitted values

a data frame

Default value

none

dataset_keys

The key variables of dataset, in key order, e.g. exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISIT), stored in the "admiral_dataset_keys" attribute. They must be variables of dataset: if any is not, a warning is issued and the keys are not set, so any keys set by a previous call are kept. An empty list, exprs(), records that the dataset has no key variables defined, which is distinct from its keys never having been set. NULL leaves keys stored by a previous call untouched.

Permitted values

list of variables created by exprs() or NULL

Default value

NULL

dataset_name

The name of the dataset, e.g. "ADVS", stored in the "admiral_dataset_name" attribute. There are no restrictions on its casing: it is stored exactly as given. NULL leaves a name stored by a previous call untouched, so re-keying a dataset does not lose its name.

Permitted values

character scalar or NULL

Default value

NULL

dataset_class

The ADaM dataset class, stored in the "admiral_dataset_class" attribute. This is the ADaM class of the dataset, not its R class (which is admiral_df). It must be given in upper case, as listed below. "TTE" is the time-to-event subclass of "BDS". "ADDL", "MDBDS", "MDTTE", and "MDOCCDS" are the medical device classes (device-level, and the device versions of "BDS", "TTE", and "OCCDS"). The class is not checked against the variables of dataset. NULL leaves a class stored by a previous call untouched.

Permitted values

"ADSL", "BDS", "OCCDS", "TTE", "ADDL", "MDBDS", "MDTTE", "MDOCCDS", or NULL

Default value

NULL

Value

dataset with the admiral_df class, and the "admiral_dataset_keys", "admiral_dataset_name", and "admiral_dataset_class" attributes for those of dataset_keys, dataset_name, and dataset_class which were supplied (or had been stored by a previous call).

Details

The keys can come from anywhere: the by_vars of the derivation which produced the dataset, a dataset specification, or a hand-written list. A specification provides them as a character vector, which chr2vars() converts. {admiral} does not read specification objects itself; to use the keys defined in a {metacore} specification, extract them in the calling code, e.g. chr2vars(metacore::get_keys(spec, "ADVS")$variable).

All {admiral} dataset functions tag their output with the admiral_df class, but they do not carry the metadata through. The core {dplyr} verbs (mutate(), filter(), arrange(), select(), rename(), slice(), distinct(), joins where dataset is x, ...) restore data frame attributes, so the metadata survives those. It is not preserved by operations which build a new data frame, in particular:

  • summarise(),

  • tidyr::pivot_longer()/pivot_wider(), nest()/unnest(), complete(),

  • bind_rows() when dataset is not the first argument,

  • joins where dataset is the y (rather than the x) argument,

  • ungroup(), after group_by() or rowwise() (which themselves keep the attributes but drop the admiral_df class).

Many derivations use these internally, so metadata set at the start of a derivation pipeline is lost along the way. Set it once the dataset is finished, or re-apply this function if the dataset changes afterwards.

The keys are stored as plain variable names, so they are not updated by rename() or removed by select(): a key which is no longer in the dataset means it has changed since its keys were set.

See also

Utilities used within Derivation functions: extract_unit(), get_dataset_class(), get_dataset_keys(), get_dataset_name(), get_flagged_records(), get_not_mapped(), get_vars_query()

Examples

Tagging a dataset with its metadata

library(tibble)

advs <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~PARAMCD, ~AVISIT,    ~AVAL,
  "1",      "DIABP",  "BASELINE",    51,
  "1",      "SYSBP",  "BASELINE",   121,
  "2",      "DIABP",  "BASELINE",    79
)

advs <- admiral_df(
  advs,
  dataset_keys = exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISIT),
  dataset_name = "ADVS",
  dataset_class = "BDS"
)

get_dataset_keys(advs)
#> [[1]]
#> USUBJID
#>
#> [[2]]
#> PARAMCD
#>
#> [[3]]
#> AVISIT
#>
get_dataset_name(advs)
#> [1] "ADVS"
get_dataset_class(advs)
#> [1] "BDS"
class(advs)
#> [1] "admiral_df" "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"

Keys from a dataset specification

A dataset specification provides the keys as a character vector, which chr2vars() converts. {admiral} does not read specification objects itself, so they are extracted in the calling code; e.g. with a {metacore} specification that is metacore::get_keys():

admiral_df(
  advs,
  dataset_keys = chr2vars(metacore::get_keys(spec, "ADVS")$variable),
  dataset_name = "ADVS"
)

advs <- admiral_df(
  advs,
  dataset_keys = chr2vars(c("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISIT"))
)

# `dataset_name` was not repeated, so the name from the previous call stands
get_dataset_name(advs)
#> [1] "ADVS"

Declaring that a dataset has no key variables

An empty dataset_keys is stored all the same. It is not the same as leaving the attribute unset: it records that no key variables are defined.

advs_no_keys <- admiral_df(advs, dataset_keys = exprs())

get_dataset_keys(advs_no_keys)
#> list()
